Title: Tou en hagiois patros hemon Gregoriou archiepiskopou Thessalonikes tou Palama Homiliai tessarakonta kai mia, hon proegountai duo logoi Philotheou kai Neilou patriarchon Konstantinoupoleos; nun to proton typois ekdidomenai meta prolegomenon (transliterated from the Greek title page; the host catalogues it as Homiliai tessarakonta ...)
Creator: Gregory Palamas (c. 1296-1359), archbishop of Thessalonica; the encomia of Palamas by the patriarchs Philotheos and Neilos of Constantinople come first; first printed edition, issued by order of the patriarch of Jerusalem, with prolegomena
Publisher: Jerusalem: Press of the Holy Sepulchre (ek tes typographias tou Panagiou Taphou), 1857
Publication Date: 1857
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: the title page reads 'A857' in this scan's OCR (file line 125), that is 1857, and the imprint is Jerusalem; host record: date 1857, possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT.
Language: grc (Greek with parallel or following Latin translation; the Latin and Greek share the OCR file; see the content note)
Source: Internet Archive item gtongoispatrsym00palagoog (archive.org/details/gtongoispatrsym00palagoog), full-text file gtongoispatrsym00palagoog_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the Library thread, October 2026.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the Library thread; the OCR text follows it unchanged. Nothing was stripped, normalised, corrected, re-spaced or retyped (the long s glyph occurs 0 times and was left as found). The Google Books boilerplate page at the head of the OCR is left in place. The OCR text that follows is 2260997 bytes, 1205579 characters and 34148 lines. OCR quality sampled at the title pages and at about 5%, 50% and 95% of the file (lines 1720, 17087 and 32453): Greek polytonic clean with occasional chi-for-kappa and stray Latin letters; almost no Latin (the prolegomena are in Greek).
Content note: The first printing of forty-one homilies of Palamas in Greek, with two panegyrics of Palamas by the patriarchs Philotheos and Neilos before them and the editor's prolegomena (from file line 137). The Greek is clean polytonic. Migne's tomus 151 reprints these homilies with Latin; this is the Greek-only first edition. The file holds Palamas as preacher to a Thessalonian congregation, not the controversial treatises.
